catalyst_stack: Tesla beat Q3 delivery consensus on 2026-10-02 with 486,532 vehicles after a larger Q2 beat of 480,126 on 2026-07-02, while Q2 revenue rose 26% to $28.2 billion on 2026-07-22. Commercial Cybercab rides opened in Austin on 2026-09-03, Semi volume production started at the new Nevada plant on 2026-09-25, Megapack 3 began rolling in Brookshire on 2026-08-06, and Optimus output reached several hundred robots a week by 2026-09-25. NHTSA opened Cybercab certification audit AQ26002 on 2026-09-03 and defect petition DP26010 on 2026-10-09 over school-zone speeding, while JPMorgan cut its target to $415 from $445 on 2026-10-13. Offsets include NHTSA closing the 2022 phantom-braking probe on 2026-07-02, a $30 billion undrawn credit package on 2026-09-29, and Street PT raises from Jefferies to $400 on 2026-10-12 and Yorkville Ives’ $500 initiate on 2026-10-06.
key_assumption: NHTSA’s AQ26002 Cybercab certification audit and DP26010 school-zone petition stay investigative and do not halt unsupervised robotaxi service or force a broad ADS recall.

catalyst_grid.evidence_excerpt: Tesla said the Cybercab, a self-driving car with no steering wheel or pedals, is now available for public rides in Austin.
NHTSA closed its 2022 Tesla phantom-braking probe covering hundreds of thousands of vehicles after complaints fell sharply and no associated crashes were found.

On October 12, 2026, Jefferies raised its price target on Tesla (TSLA) to $400 from $350 while maintaining a Hold rating.
The Office of Defects Investigation opened the file, DP26010, on Friday, October 9
Cybercab certification audit (AQ26002): Opened September 3, 2026 (the same day commercial Cybercab rides began in Austin).
April 21, 2026: Musk disposed of 96,000,000 restricted shares back to the issuer (forfeiture tied to a Tornetta Decision Event)
JPMorgan cuts Tesla’s price target to $415 from $445 and lowers its Q3 delivery and margin estimates
The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has opened an investigation into roughly 1.2 million Tesla vehicles after receiving 156 complaints
But it missed badly on profit: non-GAAP earnings came in at just $0.33 per share, well short of the $0.53 analysts were looking for
